title: With the measured preference of CPV labels for many dips, TESS rates and dip counts fit a corotating-clump model with clumps in most young M dwarfs; older-star counts are inconclusive
abstract: Complex periodic variables (CPVs) are young, rapidly rotating M dwarfs with sharp dips at the rotation period. We test a published corotating-clump occurrence model with the number of dips in each light curve. We count dips at a common noise level in the folded TESS sector 56-107 curves of 126 CPVs. We remove dips from 61 young CPV curves and score them with an emulator of the visual CPV label. Relative to unchanged curves, the label probability is 0.21 for one dip, 0.48 for two, 0.80 for three and 0.94 for four or more. The published rate-only parameters predict 62% single-dip CPVs among 394 young (1-24 Myr) rapid rotators; 12% of 41 counted CPVs are single-dip (p < 2.5e-4). With the measured selection, a rate-only fit predicts the count distribution (p = 0.70), and a joint fit needs 2.6 times the published clump intensity. A host fraction below 0.85 (dipole, BHAC15 radii), 0.73 (ring), 0.56 or 0.44 (photometric radii) is excluded at 95%. Thus most young rapid rotators carry clumps in this model, and inclination, x and the label set the 14% rate. Up to 60 Myr, x explains the CPV rate (15 seen, 15.5 expected). Older and near-main-sequence cohorts have fewer CPVs than expected (2 of 3.8; 4 of 23.8). Their dip counts favour fewer hosts over fewer clumps per host in the joint model (Delta ln L 2.2-3.6), but a model-free test does not reject either. Limits: emulated vetting, dip-decomposition errors, assumed geometry and 1-13 older stars with counts. Code, TESS-derived morphology tables and aggregate results are included; Gaia-derived record tables are excluded.

(a) Common-noise dip counts of 41 young CPVs (black) and the predictions of the published rate-only clump model without dip-count selection (orange), a rate-only fit with the measured selection (green) and a joint fit to labels and counts (blue), scaled to 41 stars. (b) Profile likelihood of the fraction of young rapid rotators that host clumps, for two geometries and two radius estimates; the dashed line is the 95% limit.

The dotted line is the young mean.
